svg.title: macOS · Photo viewer / grading editor · Text tab · 1000×700
svg.desc: Mirrors App/PhotoViewerView.swift (textTab, overlayLanes, overlayRunAccessory) hosting App/Overlay/OverlayEditingPanel.swift, App/Overlay/OverlayLanesView.swift and App/Overlay/OverlayCopyField.swift — the Text page of the editor rail, rebuilt 2026-09-03 from the Claude Design handoff "Photo viewer text transitions" (Text Workflow · direction 1a: timing lives in the rail, the lanes are its read-mostly mirror). Window 1000×700; media column 660 (black), rail 340. STAGED: LL_EDITOR=<interval project with no text> LL_RAIL=text LL_TEXT=story — the design's four-layer Prague story: row 1 "Don't you think" (ID "Intro top", Character · Bounce 8→20%, Fade out 80→86%), row 2 "Prague" (Element · Fade, starts after row 1), row 3 "is worth a LITTLE visit?" (Character · Bounce, the word LITTLE charcoal inside white copy, after row 2), row 4 "visitprague.com" (Lemon, Element · Fade, after row 3 with a +2% offset, no exit). Playhead parked at 13%, so row 1 is mid-bounce: the composite shows "Don't y" with the y still dropping in; the three later layers are not on screen yet. Row 1 is selected and, here, expanded with TEXT, TYPE and REVEAL IN open (a card opens with TEXT alone; the others are a click each). MEDIA COLUMN: picture 660×495 letterboxed at y=22 in a 540 pane — the pane gave up 78pt for the lanes. Text layers composite live at the playhead through the same rasterizer the export bakes with; the SELECTED layer draws a solid accent 1.5pt outline and a "FREE · first 18 chars" badge (10/600 white on accent, 18pt capsule) 22pt above it; a selected layer that is not on screen at the playhead (before its reveal, after its exit) ghosts at 16% so the badge has a target; every other resting layer is an invisible hit area over the bake. Click a layer to select it, drag to place it (existing). TRANSPORT + LANES (top 568, padding 8/18/0): row 1 is GradeTimelineView(compact: true) — 26pt white play/pause disc with the accent glyph, the 3pt track with the 3×20 ink playhead and the rgba(43,43,46,.9) clock pill (10/600 white, tabular), then the two 26pt frame-step discs (‹ ›, 6pt gaps); play now LOOPS and advances the playhead in real time at the project's own output length (the newest blended clip's frames ÷ fps; a 14 s tour before one exists), any scrub or lane drag stops it. Row 2: end labels 10pt #6D6D72 tabular, indented to the track (34 left / 64 right). Row 3: the LANES, 18pt per lane, top lane = front layer (list order), height from the layer count (6 lanes before the block scrolls): a hairline (black 6%) at mid-height; the layer's displayName 9pt #8A8A8E right-aligned in the 26pt gutter left of the track; the BAND = the layer's on-screen span [reveal.start, exit.end ?? 1], 12pt tall, radius 6, accent when selected (with a 1.5pt white ring inside a 1pt accent ring) and accent 42% otherwise; darker heads (black 22%) mark the reveal-in and reveal-out spans inside it (a cut has no head). Trim handles at both ends (8×16 hit, ew-resize cursor): the left edge is reveal.start (dragging it breaks a link), the right edge is exit.end (only drawn with an exit on). Dragging the body moves the whole layer in time — reveal and exit together, clamped to 0…1 — and breaks its own link while its children keep following it. A LINKED layer draws a dotted 2pt accent connector from parent.reveal.end to its band start (invisible at a 0 offset, as for rows 2 and 3 here; the +2% offset on row 4 shows one) and a 14pt white disc with arrow.turn.down.right (accent, accent-50% ring) on the band start. The playhead line (1pt rgba(28,28,30,.55)) spans all lanes. Clicking a band selects the layer. RAIL (x 676, 308 inner): RailTabBar [Editor · Text · Frames · Masks] unchanged; header "Text Layers · 4 layers". LAYER ROW (38pt): grip · eye · title · (linked) 16pt capsule ⤷ accent on accent-10% · wand (accent when the layer has a reveal style or an exit) · onion skin (needs a reveal) · chevron. When the ID is set the title reads "ID · copy" with the copy at 50%. EXPANDED CARD, sections in order, 12pt side padding, 9pt gaps, hairline dividers, titles 11/600 +0.5 #6D6D72: 1 TEXT — the copy field (min 30pt, 1px black-22% border, radius 6, 14pt; multi-line, Return = newline). It is a RICH field: each run of the copy can carry its own colour, weight and underline. Placing the caret in a word (or selecting a range) opens the MINI TOOLBAR directly under the field — ink #1C1C1E bar, radius 9, 6/8 padding: the run label "“you”" 10.5pt white 65% · B 22pt square (accent when on) · U 22pt (#2C2C2E) · six 14pt swatches (White · Ink · Accent · Amber · Lemon · Charcoal; selected ring 2 white + 1.5 accent) · ✕. Typed text inherits the style of the run it lands at the end of; a run edited to nothing merges away. (The caret read-back needs macOS 15 / iOS 18; on the 14/17 floors the bar acts on the whole layer.) Then Mode (Free · Box), Size (px of the delivered file) and Angle — exactly as shipped. 2 TYPE — the font field (26pt, #F2F2F7, radius 7, the family name in its own face, an IMPORTED tag 9/700 accent on accent-10% for a face the project brought with it, ⌃⌄) opens a POPOVER list, not a menu (AppKit drops a menu label's chrome): six system faces · divider · imported faces (IMPORTED tag) · divider · "+ Import font… TTF · OTF" (square.and.arrow.down) → file importer; the file is copied into the project's fonts/ folder (ProjectArchive.transferableSubfolders), registered with CTFontManager for the process, listed by family, and the layer being edited switches to it (toast "Imported <family>"). B · I · U 26pt squares (radius 7; accent fill when on, #F2F2F7 off), alignment ≡ ☰ ≡, six 16pt swatches (the TYPE row's swatch is the LAYER colour and clears every run's own), More… (kerning / line height / paragraph / auto-size popover, unchanged). 3 INTELLIGENT PLACEMENT — unchanged and mandatory: None, the project's regions (Sky · Land or a custom mask's names), Custom → the Masks tab. 4 REVEAL IN — the header trails "start → end · duration" 10.5pt #8A8A8E tabular ("Cut · appears at 0:05:45" when no style is on). Segmented Element · Word · Character (26pt track #F2F2F7, accent fill). Style chips 24pt radius 12 11.5/600 (#F2F2F7 / accent when on): Fade · Slide · Bounce · Pop · Blur · Wipe — tapping the active chip CLEARS it (no chip = hard cut). Slide adds the From row. Stagger slider (Word/Character only) with its word readout: one at a time (<0.2) · overlapping · almost together (>0.85). Set Start / Set End 40pt (Set Start clears a link; Set End only changes the duration and keeps it). Starts: At time · After layer; with After: the parent field (⤷ displayName ⌃⌄ → popover listing the other layers except this one's own descendants, ✓ on the current) + the offset stepper − +0s + (one FRAME per step, tabular, −10%…+30%) and the footnote "Moves with its parent. Offset is measured from the parent's reveal end; negative overlaps them." Picking a parent floats the toast "Linked — starts after “…”" (28pt dark capsule over the media, 1.8 s). 5 REVEAL OUT — the header carries a 30×16 toggle (accent / #E9E9EB). Off: "Off: the text holds on screen until the end of the shoot." On (seeded at reveal.end + 30%, 6% long): unit segmented · style chips Fade · Slide · Pop · Blur · Wipe (no bounce out; tapping the active chip = hard cut at exit.end) · From for Slide · Stagger · Set Out Start / Set Out End (readouts "start → end" and the duration) · the footnote. 6 ID — one row: "ID" label (12/600, 36 wide) + a single-line field (26pt) with the placeholder "e.g. Intro top · Byline · Main message". 7 Remove Text — unchanged. Add Text 44pt (a shoot with length opens the new layer's reveal at the playhead: a 6% fade, whole element, no exit). Footnote: "Get the layout right first, then time the reveals. Drag text on the preview to place it; drag a band in the lanes to move it in time. The top layer sits in front." MODEL: OverlayAnimation = reveal (OverlayReveal: unit · style? · direction · start · end · overlap) + exit? + follows? (parent id + gap); a layer with no animation reads as a cut at 0:00 that holds. Sequencing resolves after EVERY edit (OverlayDocument.resolveFollows: reveal.start = parent.reveal.end + gap, duration kept, exit shifted by the same delta; as many passes as layers so chains resolve in any list order; cycles and dangling links dropped; removing a parent leaves its children at their resolved times). Units generalise the old per-character phases: characters as before, words = whitespace-delimited with the spaces travelling with the preceding word, element = one unit; the rasterizer draws unit by unit — Fade alpha · Slide alpha + 0.6em travel from the direction · Bounce 0.9em drop through ease-out-back · Pop scale through ease-out-back about the baseline centre · Blur alpha + a Core Image gaussian on the unit (radius 0.22em at t=0) · Wipe a left-to-right clip; the house cubic eases everything but Bounce/Pop. At any position ≥ reveal.end and < exit.start the raster is byte-identical to no animation (same cache entry). Exports bake reveal, exit and resolved times through the same compositor; the whole-shoot still bakes every layer settled. TextOverlayContent.string became runs: [TextRun] (text · colorHex? · isBold? · isUnderlined?, nil = inherit); the sidecar writes the joined string under the old key as well, so older builds read plain copy, and a plain-string sidecar decodes as one run; the spike's single band (st/d/a/b/o) decodes as a Character reveal of the same style and span. Hooks: LL_EDITOR, LL_RAIL=text, LL_TEXT=story[,toast]. Verified against the running Mac app 2026-09-03 (dark appearance on the bench; this drawing is the light window the tokens name): staging, lanes, band drag re-seating its children and breaking its link, the run toolbar on a caret with B and a swatch applied to one word, the font popover, the parent picker and offset stepper, live looping playback.
